Use case: illustration-story. Create a polished art-direction comparison sheet for "BLOCK WORLD" with THREE equally prominent side-by-side square-ish illustrated panels. Wide landscape canvas, approximately 3:2. Off-white margins and clean understated typography. Header "BLOCK WORLD" and subheading "One shared style for every Minecraft adventure". Each column is a DIFFERENT medium, not just a palette variation. Put the exact option label below its panel. Repeat the same scene in all three: Cory, a school-age boy with short brown hair, rectangular glasses, blue shirt, exploring a block-built forest at dawn beside a proud white sheep; cubic trees, grassy cube ledges and a distant square cave with cyan gems. Cory and the sheep stay recognizably the same across panels, adapted to the medium. This is a children's choose-your-own-adventure book, warm, curious and playful.
Left label "M1 · Cinematic voxel": miniature 3D cube world, tactile matte blocks with detailed pixel textures, lush atmospheric depth, warm shaft of morning sun, dramatic eye-level story composition, block-built boy and sheep.
Middle label "M2 · Pixel quest": exquisite strictly pixel-art illustrated adventure, crisp visible square pixels, deliberate clustered shading and restrained dithering, 1990s story-game background craft, detailed sprites; no smoothing, no painted brushstrokes.
Right label "M3 · Block-print comic": exuberant printed graphic adventure, bold dark contour lines, cut-block angular shapes, flat emerald/cobalt/apricot color with misregistered screenprint and halftone textures, kinetic diagonals; truly 2D, not 3D.
Avoid dreamy princess oil painting, watercolor realism, lavender-gold fairy-tale aesthetic, realistic human faces, logos, watermarks and extraneous text. Large scenes with small readable labels. No UI or buttons. This is a preview style sampler, not final story pages.

Keep child and dragon design consistent within a panel; simplify as appropriate to medium. Large readable friendly characters, suited to age three.

Middle label "R2 · Paper-cut garden": richly layered colored paper collage, visible crisp cut edges and real layer shadows, scalloped foliage, paper-built figures, bright raspberry and leaf-green with cream sky, sophisticated tactile picture book.
Right label "R3 · Wax-crayon wonder": delightfully expressive premium children's illustration with chunky wax-crayon lines, vivid oil-pastel color, visible paper tooth, loose charming shapes, flat composition, playful hand marks, no shiny modeling.
Avoid the luminous detailed lavender-and-gold princess painting aesthetic, photographic child faces, plastic 3D animation, overly huge button eyes, logos and watermarks. No text except heading and option labels. This is a choice sampler, not three consecutive story pages.

Cozy outdoor family adventure, safe and happy, clearly cartoon illustration. Keep cast small enough to read well.

Middle label "C2 · Field-journal adventure": lively pen-and-colored-pencil travel sketchbook, fine ink crosshatching, earthy colored pencil on cream paper, intimate expressive characters, carefully drawn pine needles and camping gear; scene only, no handwritten annotation or scrapbook words.

Make mediums strikingly distinct. Avoid the dreamy royal lavender-and-gold fairy-tale painting look, realistic human faces, logos, watermarks, speech bubbles or other text. Display only the title and three option labels.

Use case: illustration-story. Make a polished, imaginative art-direction comparison sheet titled "PIZZA PLANET RESCUE". Alien shape consistent across three panels, short rounded bodies, three eyes in a row, two arms, two legs; keep eyes count clear.

Right label "P3 · Cosmic comic": bold adventurous comic-book panel, saturated electric cyan and magenta against midnight navy with scarlet planet, expressive heavy ink outlines, dramatic perspective and halftone shading, energetic fun without combat; no speech bubbles.
Avoid the detailed luminous princess painting look, pastel fairy-tale watercolor, logos, watermarks, real brands and extra text. Show only main title and option labels. Three distinct mediums, not the same painting recolored. Style-exploration preview, not a final page.

Use case: illustration-story. Create a striking art-direction comparison sheet titled "THE MERMAID'S LOST SONG". THREE equal side-by-side scene panels, broad landscape approximately 3:2, refined ivory margins and exact option labels below each panel. Repeat the same gentle seaside scene across all three: Princess Ellie, a preschool girl with straight chin-length dark-brown bob, side fringe, silver tiara and lavender dress, kneels on the shore and holds a large pink spiral seashell toward a little friendly mermaid with flowing dark-teal hair, modest short-sleeved coral tunic and a turquoise fish tail, seated on a tidepool rock; one small red crab nearby, seaweed and wave curls. The mermaid's song is missing: quiet thoughtful faces and a sense of listening. Keep recognizable designs and the same cast throughout.
Left label "S1 · Sea-glass mosaic": a luxurious handmade sea-glass mosaic illustration, rounded translucent tesserae in aquamarine, cobalt and pearly cream with coral pink accents, clear outlines and elegant expressive faces built from carefully arranged small glass pieces; the entire scene including faces is mosaic, catching gentle light.
Middle label "S2 · Flowing Art Nouveau": lyrical 2D decorative story illustration, fluid sinuous ink contours, stylized looping waves and seaweed, finely patterned flat teal coral and pale-cream areas, elegant flowing shapes, ornamental framing; beautiful original family-friendly Art Nouveau composition, no realistic painting.
Right label "S3 · Risograph tidepool": wonderfully graphic two-to-three-ink risograph picture-book illustration, vivid turquoise and coral fluorescent ink over warm cream paper, grainy overlapping colors, quirky charming flat figures, confident simplified shapes and playful scalloped waves.
Distinctly different from luminous lavender-and-gold dimensional princess paintings. No photographic faces, no pinup styling, no logos or watermarks, no text except heading and labels. Aim for imaginative, beautiful, clearly contrasting style options.

Use case: illustration-story. Create a beautiful art-direction comparison sheet titled "THE WHISPERING LIBRARY". THREE equally prominent side-by-side panels in a wide landscape canvas approximately 3:2 with crisp ivory margins and exact readable option labels under each. Same scene in all three: Jeannie, a seven-year-old reader with shoulder-length brown hair and a purple dress, stands with a tiny animated quill-pen companion on her shoulder in an extraordinary library. Do not give individual worlds separate art styles.

Middle label "L2 · Etched story atlas": exquisitely detailed antique adventure-book engraving reinvented for children, fine dark-navy etched line work, stipple and crosshatching, restrained copper and emerald spot color on warm ivory, expressive illustrated child face, elaborate yet readable library, tiny atlas-like worlds, NO actual map labels or writing. Flat printed illustration, no painterly glow.
Right label "L3 · Graphic-novel mystery": sophisticated all-ages graphic novel illustration, cinematic perspective, assured ink lines, expressive naturally proportioned characters, deep indigo and rich teal with coral highlights, dramatic cel-shaded light, mysterious floating pages and magical world glimpses, adventurous but friendly.
